subject: Service incident: closure summary and preventative plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lee <harper.lee@datafin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service incident: closure summary and preventative plan

Hi Harper —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated the service disruption you experienced yesterday (2027-03-03). Attached is our consolidated post-incident summary and the timelines CSV. I wanted to share the highlights, the root-cause analysis at a high level, and the specific actions we are committing to for Datafin.

Executive summary
- What happened: a cascading scheduler misallocation caused our inference fleet autoscaler to allocate fewer worker pods than required for a short window, which increased request queuing and led to timeouts for higher-concurrency routes.
- Impact: ~11 minutes of elevated 5xxs and latency spikes for multi-request batches; affected Datafin’s batch scoring pipeline and a subset of API calls between 10:22–10:33 PDT.
- Status: mitigations applied and service restored; we've validated normal traffic and looked for recurrence.

Root cause (short)
- A regression in autoscaler heuristics (a change to the warm-start path) reduced headroom when a specific memory-pressure signal coincided with a spike in multi-request batches. The change passed unit tests but missed a workload regression test for sustained small-batch bursts.

Timeline (high level)
- 10:20 PDT — Traffic spike on Datafin scoring route.
- 10:22 PDT — Autoscaler begins conservative downscale due to transient memory signal; queue length increases.
- 10:27 PDT — Error rates cross alert thresholds; SRE team begins mitigation.
- 10:31 PDT — Temporary override applied; new workers provisioned.
- 10:33 PDT — Error rates return to normal; monitoring confirms healthy KPIs.

Committed actions for Datafin (what we will do)
1) Immediate: we have rolled back the heuristics change in the warm-start path for your tenant and applied a temporary autoscaler headroom override for high-concurrency routes (completed).
2) Near-term (2 weeks): add an explicit workload regression test targeting small-batch bursts and memory signal combinations; ship a fix to the autoscaler logic with Canary and canary-to-100% rollout gating.
3) Operational: enable per-route burst headroom configuration for your account so you can pin more conservative scaling for critical routes.
4) Compensation: we are prepared to discuss a one-time credit for the incident window; please confirm the preferred owner on your side for compensation discussions.

Attached: datafin-20270304-postmortem.pdf (detailed timeline, logs extracts, and test vectors); service-timeline-20270304.csv

Next steps
- If useful, I can book a 30-minute readout with your ops and platform teams this week to walk the postmortem and the planned fixes.
- Please send any specific questions or additional logs you want included in the public postmortem.

Thanks again — we take availability seriously and will do everything we can to prevent recurrence.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Harper Lee <harper.lee@datafin.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service incident: closure summary and preventative plan

Vivek —

Thanks for the rapid follow-up and the clear write-up. Two quick questions:
1) Can you confirm whether any of our persisted inputs were retried or dropped (we saw partial scoring results logged on our side)?
2) On credits — we’ll need an internal owner to sign off; is there an SLA credit policy you can reference?

Appreciate the offer for a readout — early next week would work.

Best,
Harper
Ops Lead, Datafin Inc

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lee <harper.lee@datafin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service incident: closure summary and preventative plan

Harper —

Answers inline:
1) Persisted inputs: we’ve reviewed request logs and replayed the scoring window. No requests were silently dropped at the platform layer; requests that timed out at the API layer generated 504s and were visible as failures. We captured all request IDs and latency/error codes in the attached CSV. If Datafin wants, we can provide a filtered export of the request IDs for reconciliation.
2) Credits: our standard SLA credit policy is outlined here: https://redwood.com/legal/sla-credits — for incidents where confirmed availability falls below the SLA in a billing period we offer pro rata credits. Given the short window here, we anticipate a small one-time credit; if you want, I’ll open a formal credit request on your behalf once you confirm the preferred contact and affected invoice period.

Proposed readout times: Tue 2027-03-09 09:00 PDT or Wed 2027-03-10 11:00 PDT. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Vivek

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Datafin incident — credit request & rollout plan

Folks —

Following up on the Datafin thread. Harper asked about credits and a readout. Please see the attachments (postmortem + timeline). Questions:
- Credit: recommend we offer a one-time credit equal to 0.5% of March invoice (covers the 11-minute window and operational overhead). Neha, can you confirm finance signoff and whether we need an approval from Scott (revenue ops)?
- Rollout: engineering plans to ship the autoscaler fix with a canary to Datafin tenant in two weeks and we’ll enable per-route burst headroom for Datafin immediately. Marissa, can you confirm ETA for the per-route flag and whether it requires any tenant migration?

I’m planning to send a customer-facing note with the readout invite after we have agreement on credits.

Thanks —
Vivek

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lee <harper.lee@datafin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-05T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service incident: closure summary and preventative plan

Harper —

Quick update after internal alignment:
- Credit: We will issue a one-time credit equal to 0.5% of your March invoice. I’ll open the formal credit request (HUBSPOT-23456) and loop finance; Neha will be the internal owner for this.
- Per-route headroom: Marissa confirmed the flag can be enabled for your tenant without migration; I’ve requested that be applied to your critical scoring routes by EOD 2027-03-06.
- Engineering fix: target ship date for the autoscaler logic patch is 2027-03-18 with a Datafin canary for validation.

I’ve attached the final postmortem PDF and the timeline CSV for your records. If that schedule looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 2027-03-09 09:00 PDT to review the details with our SRE and product owners.

Thanks — we appreciate your partnership and will follow up promptly with the credit request and calendar invite.

Regards,
Vivek
